Akaganeite Mineral

Akaganeite is a distinct iron oxyhydroxide mineral species, listed with formula (Fe(III),Ni(II))8(OH,O)16Cl1.25·nH2O, renamed status (Rn), and IMA number 1962-004 in the September 2026 IMA master list. The experimental abbreviation beta-FeOOH identifies the synthetic phase assignment used by the study; it does not establish the ideal IMA composition or nickel content of that preparation. This record is separate from iron element, other iron oxyhydroxide species, iron-ore commodities, and mixed waste feeds. No constituent criticality designation is inherited.

Cassiterite-polymetallic sulfide ore Primary Resource

A heterogeneous natural tin-bearing geological feed containing cassiterite and sulfide minerals, represented here by the Myanmar ore studied by Wang et al. (2025). The crushed experimental ore contained source-assigned pyrite, cassiterite, quartz, tourmaline and mica. Its mine and deposit are not specified. Crushing does not establish a processing-waste origin. This resource is distinct from cassiterite or pyrrhotite mineral species, elemental tin, a tin commodity and a produced concentrate. The study does not establish extraction from a pure mineral or properties of all ores described by this name. No criticality designation is inherited from tin.

No constituent-element criticality is inherited.

Coal beneficiation waste Secondary Resource

Heterogeneous discarded material generated by coal beneficiation, represented by gravity/flotation processing dumps of the Lviv-Volyn coal basin and the Chervonogradska central concentrating factory. This secondary resource is distinct from natural coal, coal combustion ash, mine-drainage treatment solids, a particular germanium mineral and elemental germanium. The studies describe native-community-associated laboratory leaching and an enlarged experimental cascade using selected dump samples; their compositions and outcomes are not universal waste properties. Constituent criticality, selective metal products and industrial deployment are not inferred.

Pyrite-roasting cinder Secondary Resource

Solid residue generated by roasting or calcining pyrite-bearing feed, also described as pyrite ash. The curated experiments concern calcined waste supplied by the Eti Mining Bandırma Borax Plant, Turkey, and a separately characterized, weathered pyrite-ash sample from São Domingos, Portugal. This processing residue is distinct from natural pyrite, unroasted mine tailings, smelting slag and spent sulfuric-acid-production catalyst. Its composition varies with feed, processing and weathering; neither study establishes a uniform mineral formula or commercial product specification. No criticality-list designation is inferred from constituent elements.

Skutterudite Mineral

Skutterudite is the cobalt arsenide mineral species listed as CoAs3 with grandfathered status G and original-description year 1845 in the September 2026 IMA compilation. The year is not an approval identifier. The Handbook describes cubic Im-3 symmetry and natural nickel and iron substitution. This species is distinct from nickelskutterudite, cobaltite, elemental cobalt and engineered skutterudite-type materials. Accepted microbial evidence concerns a phase-characterized, mixed Bou Azzer concentrate dominated by skutterudite; it does not establish a pure-endmember extraction rate or transfer constituent-element criticality to this mineral.

Waste X-ray films Secondary Resource

Used silver-bearing radiographic films obtained from medical facilities, comprising a gelatin-silver emulsion on a polymer base. The curated feeds are discarded X-ray films, not unused film stock, photographic processing liquids, elemental silver or all photographic wastes. Laboratory studies distinguish microbial-enzyme stripping of the emulsion from subsequent thermal production of silver metal. No constituent criticality designation or industrial deployment is inherited.
